items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: Now a lot of fellas like Picoon and my brother and my uncle and them, they didn't need that.

ctx.x: I'd like to come back to the Boling Band just for a moment. You said they had a clarinet in the band. I wonder how, was there any difference in those clarinets, in those string bands, for instance, in there would be in a, we'll say like a brass band or in a more classical band. classical band, would there be any different way of blowing it?

Well I'll tell you, there's some band that used to, some kind of play used to use a B flat and A, some used to use C clarinet, and they used to change up in between when playing, you know. If they played a certain number and was written in A, well he picked up his A clarinet. He picked up B flat, he picked up B flat clarinet, you understand? It wasn't C, he got his C clarinet. You understand? That's how it was done. Now a lot of fellas like Picoon and my brother and my uncle and them, they didn't need that. You…
Sometimes they had to pull it out the shank, out the tune, and sometimes they'd transport it.
